hypothesis: The parent's fan-out-damped cut lowers total cut but leaves crit_cross unchanged because the cut term treats every pin of a net equally; adding a pin-level criticality weight inside the expected-cut product (each pin's log-prob scaled by 1 + alpha * normalized crit rank of that pin) will pull critical pins of the same net together, lowering crit-pair cross-tier and thus TNS.
analysis: (1) Partially: crit_cross fell only on C3 (0.069→0.040) with cut also down (582→573), but total cut worsened overall (total=-0.151) and TNS barely moved (-0.003). (2) C3 drove the effect—lower crit-pair cross-tier and fewer repair flips (353→349); C1/C2 showed no crit_cross change and C1 cut rose (137→142). Mechanism consistent with pin-level weighting pulling critical pins together, but gains don't generalize. (3) Seed spread is high (seed_std=0.091; C3 per-seed -0.45 outlier)—not acceptable. (4) Gate alpha by net criticality density or anneal it, and re-test on C3-like circuits to confirm the crit_cross→TNS link before scaling.
